summary: Unify ALL THREE stacked top bars of the sports Run console into one cutting-edge surface; output a high-fidelity mock spec

understand.verticalCost: Total 144px (48+48+48). Why 3 levels persist after slice 1: Level A (page header) OUTSIDE RunMode always-mounted. Level B (command bar) INSIDE RunMode conditional but injected directly at line 1262. Level C (scene control) OUTSIDE RunMode at line 1369, between command bar and content. Mobile md:hidden doesn't collapse these horizontally—each bar has overflow-x-auto, stacking causes 3 visible rows. Desktop md+ was supposed to fold Level C into right-column body (prior IA study), but current code still renders it as top strip—that migration hasn't shipped. Three bars read as distinct levels because: (1) different bg colors (white/white/slate-50), (2) distinct control groups (navigation | roles | presentation), (3) each full-width with border-b separator.
understand.taxonomyPlacement: UNIFIED DESIGN HOME for collapsed single top bar: CONTEXT/NAV (left anchor): 'Game Day' back, game identity + live-status pill (Levels A+B merged). SURFACES (secondary): 'Ribbon', 'Scoreboard', 'Stream', 'Keys' buttons (Level A)—move to popout/drawer, not primary focus. ROLE/VIEW (primary centered): Full/Scorekeeper/Show Caller/PA segmented control (Level B)—keep prominent for multi-operator. LIVE ACTIONS (right cluster): 'Spotlight', 'Penalty', 'Send-to-device', status transitions (Levels A+B)—group right-aligned hot actions. AMBIENT STATUS: Screens-health nub (Level B)—keep right, real-time glance. PRESENTATION (body): Show-on-board scenes + Back-to-Live + Hold/Extend (Level C)—MOVE into collapsible right sidebar per prior IA, frees chrome, co-locates with Ribbon/Roster/Cues. PRIMARY GAME (hero): Score/clock/segment—center-left, full-height desktop, scrollable mobile (untouched).
redundancies: Mode switch ('Run game'/'Set up') in Level A appears before command bar, but role views only exist in run mode—gate surface buttons (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys) to run mode only, or surface view picker in setup for consistency.
Status chip logic duplicated: Level A (implied before bars) and Level B (explicit STATUS_CHIP in RunCommandBar:22-28)—consolidate to single status pill in command bar, remove page-level duplicate.
Scene-recall (Level C) is separate control hierarchy from game state—belongs with other presentation/surfaces in right column (per prior IA study design), not as top strip.
Spotlight button intent ambiguous (what surface? home/away/sponsor?)—clarify in docs and surface visibility constraints.
'Send-to-device' button duplicates Share modal that opens elsewhere (page.tsx:1285-1357)—consolidate to single integration point.

SurfaceHealthPills component embedded inside RunCommandBar—if it grows (detailed health, multi-screen preview), extract to dedicated pill row; current summary-only mode is fine but pattern should be documented for consistency.

references.name: Linear — "How we redesigned the Linear UI" (inverted-L chrome, elevation, accent rationing)
references.whatToSteal: A LAYERED single header: one fixed identity/context strip plus a contextual sub-row that changes per view (list/board/timeline) — they explicitly designed multiple header levels for different contexts but kept them aligned to one grid. Steal the two key moves for our Level A+B merge: (1) ration the accent color — use indigo ONLY on the active role segment and the LIVE pulse, everything else neutral, so the eye instantly finds 'what's hot'; (2) use elevation (LCH/oklch surface tiers: background→foreground→panel→dialog) instead of borders to separate context zones in the bar — the current 3 stacked bars read as noise precisely because each is a bordered box; one bar with subtle elevation steps reads as hierarchy.

references.name: Linear — command-model / conceptual model (contextual commands, multi-path actions)
references.whatToSteal: Every action reachable 3 ways (button + shortcut + Cmd-K palette) following ONE pattern, and the command menu surfaces context-relevant commands FIRST. For our console: keep the high-frequency live actions as visible buttons, but add a Cmd-K 'Run palette' that surfaces game-context commands first (Spotlight, Send-to-device, Show: Halftime Board, Celebrate: Goal, set Final). This lets us move medium-frequency controls (Stream popout, Keys, Set-up mode) OUT of the visible bar into the palette without burying them — the palette IS their second home. Also steal their 'minimal-choice' rule: only title+status are required; everything else optional/discoverable — i.e. the bar shows the 5 things that matter, the rest is one keystroke away.

references.name: Arc browser — chrome reimagined (command bar replaces URL bar, Little Arc, gradient identity)
references.whatToSteal: The Command Bar pattern: a single elevated input that absorbs nav + search + actions, so the visible chrome can shrink to almost nothing. Two adaptable ideas: (1) collapse the four 'surface-open' buttons (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys) into ONE 'Open ▾' overflow control on the bar (these are open/popout, not live game actions — they don't deserve four always-visible slots, the Figma lesson notwithstanding because they're low-frequency); (2) 'match the interface to the task's weight' — the Set-up vs Run mode switch is a heavyweight context change, so make it a clear segmented switch on the LEFT of the bar (like Arc's spaces), not a button competing with live actions on the right.

references.name: Figma UI3 'bring the top bar back' forum (cautionary: don't bury contextual tools)
references.whatToSteal: The anti-pattern to AVOID: Figma moved contextual tools into overflow '…' menus and the right panel; users revolted because frequently-used controls became un-discoverable and added clicks mid-task. The binding rule for our redesign: show frequently-used LIVE controls (status transitions, Spotlight, Penalty when active) directly on the bar; reserve overflow ONLY for low-frequency open/popout/config (Stream, Keys, Set-up). Under live game pressure, hunting in a menu is a failure. This is the guardrail that keeps our consolidation from over-collapsing.

references.name: vMix Control Surface — broadcast preview/program two-column + numbered fast-trigger
references.whatToSteal: The two-column Preview/Program desk (which the approved body already adopts) plus the live-trigger ergonomics: most-frequent sources drag to the front, one-button 'Take', modifier-held variants, and a clear Program (on-air) bus. For our bar+body: treat the right column's Show-on-board scenes like a Program bus — the currently-live scene gets an unmistakable on-air treatment (the tally pattern below), and 'Back to Live' is the always-present 'Take' equivalent. Muscle-memory + split-second response beats menu nav — argues for visible scene tiles and visible celebrate cues, not a palette, in the BODY.

references.name: Carbon Design System — status-indicator pattern (living status, severity roll-up, badge counts)
references.whatToSteal: Make AMBIENT status a first-class but quiet element: combine shape+color+label+motion for the LIVE chip (red dot + pulse + 'LIVE' label = WCAG-safe, instantly glanceable). For 8/8 screens health, use a compact badge with severity roll-up — show GREEN '8/8' normally, but if any screen drops, the badge goes amber/red ('7/8') and becomes the highest-severity color so it pulls the eye only when it matters. Hard rule they state: >5–6 indicators taxes the user — which is exactly why our 3 stacked bars feel noisy; consolidate to ≤5 visible status/action affordances.

references.name: Command palette: past/present/future (Superhuman → Linear → Raycast lineage)
references.whatToSteal: The command palette as the universal 'everything is one keystroke away' surface (Cmd-K) that lets the visible UI stay minimal — the through-line from Superhuman to Raycast. For our console it's the pressure-release valve: it justifies pulling Set-up/Stream/Keys/role-switch out of the always-visible bar because they remain instantly reachable. Pair with Linear's contextual-results idea so 'Half' types to Halftime, 'Spot' to Spotlight — fast for the power operator, invisible for the casual one.

techniques: CONTEXTUAL SINGLE TOP BAR (Linear inverted-L): collapse Level A + Level B into ONE bar with a fixed-left zone (back-to-GameDay chip + game identity + LIVE status chip) and a fixed-right zone (live actions), with the role segment centered. The bar's content is contextual — it shows Run-mode controls in Run, Set-up controls in Set-up — but it stays ONE physical row, never stacks.

ELEVATION OVER BORDERS (Linear LCH/oklch surface tiers): the current 3 bars read as noise because each is a bordered box. Replace with one bar on a single elevated surface; separate zones with subtle background-tier shifts + spacing, not borders/dividers. Honors mobile-perf (no blur on always-mounted chrome) — use solid oklch tiers, not backdrop-filter.

SINGLE ACCENT, RATIONED (Linear): indigo appears ONLY on the active role segment and the share/primary action; LIVE = red pulse; everything else neutral slate. This makes 'what's live' and 'what view am I in' the two things the eye finds instantly — the exact hierarchy the operator says is missing.

STATUS AS A LIVING ELEMENT (Carbon): the LIVE/Halftime/Final chip uses shape+color+label+motion (pulsing dot) so game state is glanceable from across a gym; it doubles as the status-transition trigger (tap chip → Halftime/Final menu) so 'identity' and 'status control' merge into one affordance instead of two bar regions.

SEVERITY-ROLL-UP HEALTH NUB (Carbon): the 8/8 screens nub stays quiet green normally and only escalates to amber/red + count when a screen drops — ambient status that pulls attention solely when it matters, satisfying the ≤5-indicators rule.

SEGMENTED CONTEXT SWITCH, NOT TABS (Apple HIG / Mews): Run vs Set-up is a true segmented control on the far left (same content, different mode = segmented, per the pattern guidance); Full/Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA is the role segmented control centered. Two segmented controls operating at genuinely different levels (mode vs view) coexist cleanly — exactly the 2025 guidance.

OVERFLOW / 'OPEN' MENU FOR LOW-FREQUENCY SURFACES (Arc + Figma guardrail): collapse Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys (open-popout, not live actions) into ONE 'Open ▾' control on the bar. Per the Figma lesson, NEVER bury live game controls — overflow is reserved strictly for open/popout/config that the operator touches rarely.

COMMAND PALETTE AS PRESSURE-RELEASE (Linear/Superhuman/Raycast): add a Cmd-K Run palette surfacing context commands first (Spotlight, Send-to-device, Show scenes, Celebrate cues, set Final). It lets the visible bar stay minimal because every demoted control is one keystroke away — the operator never loses access, just visual clutter.

TWO-COLUMN BROADCAST DESK WITH AN ON-AIR/TALLY TREATMENT (vMix): the approved body keeps Game Control (left) + Presentation (right); Level C's Show-on-board scenes fold into the right column as a Program bus where the LIVE scene gets an unmistakable on-air (tally) outline + 'Back to Live' acting as the 'Take'. Visible tiles, not a menu — live cueing needs muscle memory.

MOTION/TRANSITION POLISH, RESTRAINED (Linear 'imperceptible polish'): segment-thumb slides between role/mode states; the LIVE dot pulses; scene tile crossfades its on-air ring on take. Promote with will-change/contain so the first frame doesn't stall on a phone — and gate any decorative blur to md: per the project's mobile-perf standard.

MOBILE = SINGLE FULL-BLEED DECK (existing md:contents constraint preserved): on phones the one bar becomes a sticky compact header (identity + LIVE chip + Open ▾ + Cmd-K), the role segment scrolls into the deck, and the two columns linearize — no second/third bar ever appears on mobile.
topbarPatterns: THREE-ZONE GRID, ONE ROW (the merge of A+B): LEFT = context/nav (back-to-GameDay chip · Run/Set-up segmented switch · game identity · LIVE status chip that is also the status-transition trigger). CENTER = role segmented control (Full/Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA). RIGHT = live + ambient (Spotlight · Penalty[conditional] · health nub · Send-to-device · 'Open ▾' surfaces overflow · Cmd-K). One physical bar replaces both Level A and Level B.

DEMOTE BY FREQUENCY, NOT BY IMPORTANCE: keep on-bar = anything touched DURING a live play (status transitions, Spotlight, Penalty-when-active, Send-to-device, health). Move to 'Open ▾' overflow = open/popout/config touched between plays (Ribbon, Scoreboard, Stream, Keys/shortcuts). Move into the BODY's right column = Presentation (Show-on-board scenes, Celebrate cues) per the approved two-column desk — Level C disappears as a top strip.

MERGE IDENTITY + STATUS + STATUS-CONTROL into one affordance: instead of 'game name' (Level A) and a separate status chip + Halftime/Final buttons (Level B), the LIVE chip shows state AND opens the transition menu on tap. One element, three jobs — removes a whole cluster from the bar.

COLLAPSE FOUR SURFACE BUTTONS INTO ONE OVERFLOW: Ribbon · Scoreboard · Stream · Keys become a single 'Open ▾' (or a popout icon) menu — four always-visible slots reduced to one, freeing the right cluster for genuinely live actions. Each item also lives in Cmd-K so power users never open the menu.

NEVER STACK — OVERFLOW INSTEAD OF WRAP: on narrow widths the bar must overflow into the 'Open ▾' menu and Cmd-K (or horizontal-scroll the center segment), but it must NEVER spawn a second row. The 3-stacked-bars problem is solved only if the invariant 'exactly one chrome row' holds at every breakpoint.

ELEVATION + RATIONED ACCENT FOR INSTANT HIERARCHY: one elevated surface, zones separated by spacing + subtle oklch tier shifts (no borders), accent reserved for the active role segment + the LIVE pulse + the primary share action. This is what converts 'three levels of shit with no hierarchy' into a bar where the eye lands on mode → role → live-state in that order.

CONTEXT-AWARE BAR CONTENTS: the same single bar swaps its center/right contents by mode — Run shows role-segment + live actions; Set-up shows save/preview/identity-edit. Following Linear's layered-header idea, the FRAME is constant (left identity, right cluster) so it never feels like a different page, only the contextual middle changes.
understand.recommendation: Collapse Level A + Level B into ONE contextual top bar built on a three-zone grid, and let the approved two-column desk absorb Level C — keeping the invariant 'exactly one chrome row at every breakpoint.' THE BAR (one row, never stacks): LEFT zone = context/nav — a back-to-GameDay chip, a Run/Set-up segmented switch, the game identity, and a LIVE status chip that doubles as the status-transition trigger (tap → Halftime/Final), merging three former elements into one. CENTER zone = the role segmented control (Full/Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA). RIGHT zone = live + ambient actions — Spotlight, Penalty (conditional), the severity-roll-up screens-health nub (quiet green '8/8', escalates only on drop), Send-to-device, an 'Open ▾' overflow that holds the four low-frequency surface popouts (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys), and a Cmd-K Run palette. ROUTING (nothing dropped): live game controls stay visible on the bar (Figma's hard lesson — never bury what's used mid-play); open/popout/config demote to 'Open ▾' but remain one keystroke away in Cmd-K; Presentation (Show-on-board scenes + Celebrate cues) moves into the body's right column as a Program/tally bus where the live scene wears an unmistakable on-air ring and 'Back to Live' acts as the broadcast 'Take'. POLISH (the 'fine→most elegant' jump): one elevated surface with oklch tier shifts instead of bordered boxes; a single rationed accent (indigo on the active role segment + primary action only; red pulse = LIVE); shape+color+label+motion on the status chip for across-the-gym glanceability; restrained motion (sliding segment thumb, pulsing LIVE dot, scene-tile tally crossfade) promoted with will-change/contain. CONSTRAINTS honored: reuse RunCommandBar/RunStatusControl/ShowControlPanel/SurfaceHealthPills as-is (layout + hierarchy only, no logic rewrite); mobile stays the single full-bleed md:contents deck with the bar as a sticky compact header (identity + LIVE + Open ▾ + Cmd-K) and the segments scrolling into the deck; NO blur on always-mounted chrome (mobile-perf standard) — solid oklch surfaces only. Next step is a high-fidelity approval mock of this single-bar three-zone layout (desktop + mobile) for Greg's sign-off before any code. Current console code reviewed: /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/sports/[gameId]/RunCommandBar.tsx (and siblings ShowControlPanel.tsx, SurfaceHealthPills.tsx, page.tsx).

designs.oneLineSummary: Single elegant unified top bar (context + role + live actions) replaces three stacked levels; two-column broadcast desk (Game Control left, Presentation right) with Level C scenes folded into the body — instantly glanceable hierarchy, rationed accent, ambient-status roll-up.
designs.topBar: ONE UNIFIED CHROME ROW (48px, never stacks). THREE ZONES: LEFT (back-to-GameDay chip, Run/Setup segmented switch, game identity + LIVE status pill that is also the transition trigger), CENTER (role segmented control: Full/Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA), RIGHT (Spotlight, Penalty conditional, screens health nub with severity roll-up, Send-to-device, Open surfaces menu, Cmd-K palette). VISUAL HIERARCHY: Indigo accent ONLY on active role segment and LIVE pulse (red 600 animate-pulse); everything else neutral slate. Status chip uses shape+color+label+motion so game state is glanceable across a gym. Surfaces menu (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys) demoted to Open menu overflow — low-frequency open/popout doesn't deserve four visible slots. Severity-roll-up health nub: quiet green normally, escalates to amber/red only on screen drop so it pulls attention solely when it matters. One oklch elevated surface, zones separated by spacing and subtle tier shifts (no borders) — replaces the three bordered boxes that created the noise.
designs.bodyLayout: TWO-COLUMN BROADCAST DESK (desktop md+, inherited from prior IA approval). LEFT COLUMN = GAME CONTROL (scoreboard hero, clock control, per-side stats increments — untouched logic, exact same RunInteractiveScoreboard component). RIGHT COLUMN = PRESENTATION (Show-on-board scenes fold here from Level C, replacing the top strip — scene tiles, Back-to-Live, Hold/Extend buttons; ribbon live preview; celebrate cues inline; ribbon and roster as collapsible accordions). MOBILE (md:hidden): single full-bleed scrolling deck (score+clock sticky at top, ribbon preview, roster, cues below, pinned bottom status bar), runs at 320px width — one chrome row at the top, everything below scrolls as one unit.

SPOTLIGHT: RIGHT zone, always visible when mode=run (fires onHighlights callback)

OPEN SURFACES: RIGHT zone, overflow menu holding Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys (four low-frequency buttons demoted to one menu item)
CMD-K PALETTE: RIGHT zone, Run command palette surfacing Spotlight/Send-to-device/Show-scenes/Celebrate-cues/Set-Final contextually

designs.motionAndPolish: RESTRAINED CUTTING-EDGE POLISH (no blur on always-mounted chrome, mobile-perf compliant). ONE surface with oklch tier shifts instead of borders (elevation via subtle background color steps, zero blur). LIVE DOT: pulsing red (animate-pulse 1.5s cubic-bezier) so game state is felt across a gym. SEGMENT THUMB: smooth slide-transition when role changes (will-change:transform, contain:layout). SCENE-TILE on-air: crossfade to indigo outline + ON-AIR label when taken to board. HEALTH NUB: immediate color-shift (no animation) when a screen drops — severity escalation pulls the eye only on failure. PENALTY BADGE: counts update live as operator adds/clears (no stagger). All interactive elements use standard 200ms transition-colors for hover/active states. Typography: single font (Anthropic Sans), two weights only (400 regular, 500 bold), no gradients or drop shadows. Tailwind 4 tokens for spacing/colors (slate-100 through slate-900 for neutral hierarchy, indigo-600 for accent, red-600 for LIVE, green-600 for healthy, amber-500 for warning). Gap sizing uses 1.5 (6px) between zone elements on the bar so nothing feels cramped.
designs.whyAmazing: GLANCEABILITY: The eye lands on mode (Run/Setup) -> role (Full/Score/Show/PA) -> live state (LIVE pulse) in that order because accent is rationed to exactly those three affordances. No competing visual weight, no noise. CONTROL DENSITY SOLVED: Three stacked 48px bars (144px overhead) become one 48px bar, freeing 96px for the game-critical scoreboard on narrower laptops and tablets. Operator gets the entire display instead of 3 layers of overlapping controls. BROADCAST WORKFLOW HONORED: The two-column desk (Game Control left, Presentation right) mirrors every professional broadcast surface (vMix, Daktronics, ScoreVision) — muscle memory transfers from existing sports operators. Scene tiles are visible tiles, not a hidden menu, because live cueing needs instant tactile response under game pressure. HIERARCHY CLEAR: One elevated bar on a white surface (no borders) reads instantly as "the chrome that controls the game." Level C scenes now live in the body where they logically belong (with the ribbon/roster — all presentation) instead of as a third separate toolbar. MOBILE SURVIVES: Single full-bleed deck (width stays 320px, chrome stays one row at top) lets the phone operator run the game one-handed without scrolling, as requested. REUSE INTACT: Every existing component (RunCommandBar, RunStatusControl, ShowControlPanel, SurfaceHealthPills, CueLaunchpad) is reused as-is — only layout/hierarchy changes, zero logic rewrites.
risks: COMMAND-K DISCOVERABILITY: Demoting Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys to Open menu + Cmd-K requires the operator to know Cmd-K exists. Mitigation: surface a hint on first-time load (toast + onboarding checklist), make Cmd-K the topmost item in the Run palette, document in shortcuts help (already exists).

OVERFLOW MENU HABITUATION: Four always-visible buttons (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys) become one menu item. If the operator touches these mid-game (which is rare for Ribbon/Stream/Keys but frequent for Scoreboard parity checks), the extra click could feel like a regression. Mitigation: Cmd-K surfaces all four instantly — train operators to Cmd-K + 'Sco' for Scoreboard; the menu item is the 'emergency pull' fallback.

SCENE TILE SCROLLING ON NARROW WIDTHS: The Show-on-board scene tiles (Halftime/Lineup/Sponsors/ThisWeek/Countdown) are five buttons in a row. On a 12-inch iPad in landscape (900px), they fit; on a 10-inch tablet (700px body width), the row may overflow and require horizontal scroll. Mitigation: truncate scene names (Halftime → 'HT', Lineup → 'LU'), or stack to two rows on md: breakpoint. Test on iPad Air in landscape (primary target) — if it scrolls, redesign to 3-button front row + 'More ▾' menu.

SEVERITY ROLL-UP HEALTH NUB: Showing only '8/8' green normally, then escalating to '7/8' amber, relies on the operator noticing the color + number change. If a screen silently fails and the operator doesn't glance at the nub, they won't know. Mitigation: keep the summary-only nub (per project spec), but add an optional SurfaceHealthPills detail view (click nub -> detailed health modal listing all screens + connectivity status). Also add a toast/banner if health drops during a live game.

MOBILE DECK HEIGHT: The single-column mobile deck stacks scene tiles + ribbon preview + roster + cues. On a 320px iPhone the deck grows tall, and the operator might scroll past the pinned score+clock without realizing it and miss a live event. Mitigation: score+clock must be sticky/fixed position at the top on mobile (already is via md:contents pattern), and the rest (ribbon/roster/cues) is scrollable below. Test on iPhone 12 (375px) and confirm the deck doesn't exceed 2 screen-heights.

CONTEXT-AWARE BAR CONTENTS (Setup vs Run mode): The bar's center/right zones are supposed to swap between Run-mode controls (role segment, live actions) and Setup-mode controls (save/preview/identity-edit). If the mode-swap logic is missed or inconsistently implemented, the operator sees half-relevant controls in Setup, which feels like a product bug. Mitigation: treat the bar as a controlled component per the Context pattern — RunMode and SetupMode each pass their own context object (pills, status buttons, etc.) to a unified bar wrapper, no branching in the bar itself.

ROLE SEGMENT IN SETUP MODE: The role segmented control (Full/Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA) is meaningful only in Run mode. In Setup mode, the operator doesn't have distinct roles — they're always in 'Full' setup. If the role segment is visible in Setup, it's confusing. Mitigation: hide the role segment in Setup mode (replace with a breadcrumb or 'Setup mode' label), show it only when mode=run.

LIVE STATUS PILL AS TRANSITION TRIGGER: The status pill doubles as both an indicator and a tap-to-transition affordance (tap -> Halftime/Final menu). This violates the 'one control, one job' rule and might confuse operators who expect just a label. Mitigation: make the pill's affordance explicit — add a small '⌄' chevron icon on the right of the pill to signal 'this is tappable', or add a tooltip on hover ('Tap to advance game').

COLORS IN DARK MODE: The mockup uses a light-mode palette (white background, slate grays, indigo primary). If VenueOS ships with dark-mode support, the oklch tier shifts and the status chip colors (red-50 bg, red-text for LIVE) may not work in dark mode. Mitigation: define a dark-mode color ramp separately (red-900 bg, red-200 text for LIVE in dark), test the full bar in both modes before shipping.

designs.directionName: rail-plus-bar: unified top bar with left rail and two-column broadcast desk

No blur on always-mounted chrome (solid oklch surfaces, mobile-perf safe). Will-change containment on interactive elements prevents first-frame stall.
designs.whyAmazing: The three stacked bars read as noise because each is a bordered box competing for attention. The unified bar sits on one elevated surface with zones separated by spacing and rationed accent color (indigo ONLY on active role + primary action). The LIVE status chip has shape (pill) + color (red) + label (LIVE) + motion (pulse) for across-the-gym glanceability. The status chip also opens the transition menu on tap, merging identity display + state control into one affordance. The two-column broadcast desk mirrors professional consoles (vMix, Daktronics) with Game Control (left) and Presentation (right) co-located, live scenes getting unmistakable on-air tally rings, and Back-to-Live as the always-available panic button. Severity-roll-up health means the screens nub stays quiet green until something breaks, preserving operator attention. The result: a single visual hierarchy, instant understanding of mode/role/state, and broadcast-grade ergonomics that feel professional and elegant.

CENTER ZONE (20%): Role segmented control (Full/Scorekeeper/Show/PA). RIGHT ZONE (62%): Spotlight + Penalty + Health nub + Send-to-device + Open surfaces dropdown + Command palette. designs.motionAndPolish: ONE elevated surface with oklch tier shifts (no bordered boxes). RATIONED ACCENT: indigo (#4f46e5) ONLY on active role segment + primary send action, neutral slate elsewhere. LIVE status: red dot + 'LIVE' label + pulsing ring (animate-pulse 1.5s). Role segment-thumb slides (transition-colors 150ms). Scene tile crossfades on-air ring (border glow, will-change: border-color). Health nub escalates color on drop (red animation). Spotlight/Send subtle hover lift (hover:bg-indigo-50/amber-50, no shadow). All motion promoted with will-change/contain (no blur on always-mounted chrome, solid oklch surfaces). designs.whyAmazing: Chrome almost disappears (ONE thin bar replaces three boxed tiers). Hierarchy instant (back anchor | identity | role center | live actions right). LIVE status glanceable across a gym (red pulsing dot + label + kerning unmistakable), doubles as status-change entry point. Every frequently-used control stays visible (Spotlight, Penalty, Send); low-frequency surfaces demote to Open dropdown + Cmd-K (one keystroke away). Two-column desk mirrors broadcast software (Game Control left | Presentation right), mental model matches vMix/Daktronics/ScoreVision. Scene tiles with tally rings + Back-to-Live feel like real Program bus (not a menu). Motion imperceptible but alive (segment thumb slides, LIVE dot pulses, scene tiles glow on take). Accent rationed (indigo only where it matters), eye finds 'what mode am I in' and 'what action is hot' instantly. Mobile stays full-bleed single-deck with sticky compact header (identity + LIVE + Open + Cmd-K), no chrome sprawl, same hierarchy on 390px and 1440px screens.
risks: Cmd-K not fast/discoverable: operators revert to hunting Open dropdown. Mitigation: always show Cmd-K, context-surface top 5 commands, keep <100ms launch.
Scene tiles clickable during live play could accidentally take scene on-air. Mitigation: add 0.5s hold-to-confirm or gate behind modal.
Health nub severity roll-up masks screen drop if operator doesn't glance between plays. Mitigation: on-air freeze triggers modal alert + sound.
Two-column layout tight on ultrawide (1920x1200): 800px right column feels narrow. Mitigation: responsive scaling (right grows to 900-1000px on 1920+).
Role segmented control prominent; misclick mid-stress switches views mid-play. Mitigation: view switch doesn't reset game state, or add confirmation if leaving Full during live.
Show-on-board scenes visible but could overwhelm on tablets (4-5 tiles + controls fill 150px). Mitigation: horizontal scroll on sm: or collapse to dropdown.

Cmd-K adds complexity; if not obvious/fast, operators stick to visible buttons. Mitigation: always show Cmd-K affordance, surface shortcut hints (? key), ensure top 3-5 commands are play-time relevant.
LIVE status chip is both indicator AND button (tap to transition); ambiguous tap zone. Mitigation: make entire chip clickable, clear hover state (bg-red-100), tooltip 'Tap to change status'.
Health nub small target (40x28px) on mobile; operator might miss under stress. Mitigation: expand popover from nub (not modal), easier target.

Low-frequency controls (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Keys/Stream/Set-up) in Open dropdown; poor organization makes them hard to find. Mitigation: sort by frequency (Ribbon > Scoreboard > Stream > Keys, Set-up bottom), add icons, flat list.

synthesis.chosenDirection: MERGE — "One Smart Bar" (Direction 1) as the spine, fused with the vMix Program-bus tally treatment from Direction 2/3 for the right-column Presentation. Final name: **One Smart Bar + Broadcast Desk**. A single 48px unified chrome row (three zones: Context/Nav · Role · Live+Ambient) replaces all three stacked bars; the approved two-column body (Game Control left | Presentation right) absorbs Level C scenes as a Program bus with on-air tally; mobile stays the single full-bleed md:contents deck with the bar as a sticky compact header. This is the exact recommendation the phase-1 study lands on, and Direction 1 is the cleanest expression of it — I take its bar + body wholesale and graft on the on-air-tally / Back-to-Live="Take" ergonomics that Directions 2 and 3 articulate better, because live scene cueing is the one place "feels like a real broadcast console" pays off.
synthesis.rationale: Why this merge and not any single direction verbatim: all three directions are the SAME architecture (one three-zone bar + two-column desk) — they only differ in framing and in two details worth cherry-picking. (1) The bar: I take Direction 1's bar wholesale because it already EXISTS in code — RunCommandBar.tsx is the exact three-zone shell (identity+chip left, role segment center, live+ambient right) the study prescribes, and SurfaceHealthPills already ships a `summary` nub mode wired into it. Zero rewrite; the redesign is layout/hierarchy + folding Level C, not new components. (2) The Presentation column: I graft Direction 2/3's on-air TALLY treatment + Back-to-Live-as-"Take" onto ShowControlPanel, because the operator runs scenes under game pressure and a vMix-style Program bus (live scene wears an unmistakable on-air ring; Back-to-Live is the always-present panic) is the single biggest "this feels professional" lever — and ShowControlPanel already has the tile/take/hold/extend logic; it just needs to render as a vertical column instead of a horizontal strip. (3) I REJECT the heavier Cmd-K-first framing of Direction 3 for slice 1: the Figma cautionary tale in the study is explicit — never bury live controls, and Cmd-K demands discoverability the operator hasn't been trained on. Cmd-K is valuable but it's a Phase-2 pressure-release valve, not a launch dependency. Spotlight/Penalty/Send/status stay as visible buttons; only the four low-frequency surface popouts (Ribbon/Scoreboard/Stream/Keys) demote to one "Open ▾" menu. This honors the study's "demote by FREQUENCY not importance" rule and keeps slice 1 shippable without a new palette subsystem. Net: maximum reuse (RunCommandBar, RunStatusControl, ShowControlPanel, SurfaceHealthPills, RunInteractiveScoreboard all reused as-is or layout-only), one chrome row at every breakpoint, broadcast muscle-memory honored, mobile-perf compliant (no blur on always-mounted chrome).
synthesis.topBarSpec:
UNIFIED COMMAND BAR — ONE PHYSICAL ROW, NEVER STACKS, at every breakpoint.

DIMENSIONS & SURFACE
- Height: 48px content (py-2 = 8px top/bottom on a 40px min-touch control row). `shrink-0`. Border-bottom 1px slate-200. NO border between zones — separation is spacing + a single subtle elevation step.
- Surface: solid white (`bg-white`), NO backdrop-blur (always-mounted chrome → mobile-perf guard). One oklch elevated tier; zones read as hierarchy via spacing + the rationed accent, not boxes.
- Horizontal padding: px-3 (mobile) / px-4 (sm+). Inter-element gap: 1.5 (6px) within a zone; zones separated by `ml-auto` push (LEFT/CENTER hug start, RIGHT cluster hugs end).
- Overflow rule: on narrow widths the bar `overflow-x-auto`s the CENTER segment and collapses RIGHT into the Open ▾ menu — it MUST NEVER wrap to a second row. Invariant: exactly one chrome row.

ZONE LEFT — CONTEXT / NAV (hugs start, shrink-0, min-w-0)
1. Back-to-GameDay chip — 40px square ghost button, ArrowLeft 18px, slate-500 → hover bg-slate-100. Navigates /[schoolId]/sports. (Lives in the page header today; pulled into the bar's left edge.)
2. Run/Setup segmented switch — pill segmented control, bg-slate-100 rounded-xl p-0.5; two segments "Run" (Play icon) / "Set up" (gear). Active segment = white bg + shadow-sm; Run segment shows a green pulse dot when status=LIVE. This is a heavyweight CONTEXT change (Arc "spaces" pattern), so it sits far-left, never competing with live actions.
3. Game identity — 13px font-bold slate-900, truncate max-w-[160px]/[220px sm], title= full name.
4. LIVE status chip — inline-flex pill, px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full, 11px font-black uppercase tracking-widest, 1px border. Color ramp (existing STATUS_CHIP map): SCHEDULED slate, PRE_GAME amber, LIVE red-50/red-700 + dot `bg-red-500 animate-pulse`, HALFTIME blue, FINAL slate-800/white. Leading 8px dot carries shape+color+motion for across-the-gym glanceability. The chip DOUBLES as the status-transition trigger: a 9px chevron (⌄) suffix signals tappable; tap opens the RunStatusControl transition menu (Go Live / Halftime / Final with hold-to-confirm). aria-live=polite. Tooltip: "Tap to advance game state."

ZONE CENTER — ROLE (the one centered element)
5. Role segmented control — bg-slate-100 rounded-xl p-0.5; segments Full / Scorekeeper / Show Caller / PA. Active = `bg-indigo-600 text-white shadow-sm`; inactive = slate-600 hover slate-900. 40px min-height per segment, 13px font-bold. Thumb slides on change (transition-colors 150ms, will-change:transform, contain:layout). HIDDEN in Setup mode (replaced by a quiet "Setup mode" label) — roles are a Run-only concept. INDIGO appears ONLY here + on the primary Send action; this is the rationing that makes "which view am I in" the second thing the eye finds.

ZONE RIGHT — LIVE + AMBIENT (ml-auto, gap-1.5, shrink-0)
6. Spotlight — 40px square ghost, Star 18px, slate-500 → hover bg-amber-50/amber-700. Visible only when mode=run. Fires onHighlights().
7. Penalty (conditional, penalty-box sports only) — pill, ⏱ glyph + count badge. count=0: ghost slate-500 → hover amber. count>0: `bg-amber-500 text-amber-950` with a dark count badge. Fires onPenalty().
8. Screens-health nub — SurfaceHealthPills summary mode (already built). Quiet: 8px green dot + "8/8" (tabular-nums) in a ghost button. Escalates IMMEDIATELY (no animation) to amber dot ("7/8", showing-other) or red dot (frozen/offline) — severity roll-up, pulls the eye only on failure. Tap → popover with the full dark pill row + per-screen live-preview drawer (existing).
9. Send-to-device — 40px square ghost, ExternalLink 18px, slate-500 → hover bg-indigo-50/indigo-700 (the one other indigo touchpoint). Opens the role-link QR share sheet.
10. Open ▾ — single overflow menu pill (slate-500, ChevronDown). Holds the four LOW-FREQUENCY surface popouts: Ribbon (/ribbon/:id), Scoreboard (/board/:id), Stream (copy overlay URL, run-only), Keys (shortcuts modal, run-only). Sorted by frequency: Scoreboard > Ribbon > Stream > Keys. Four always-visible slots → one menu item; nothing dropped. (Cmd-K, Phase 2, will surface these too.)

ACCENT DISCIPLINE: indigo-600 ONLY on active role segment + Send hover; red-600 = LIVE pulse; green/amber/red = health severity. Everything else neutral slate-100→900. Two font weights (400/500-ish via font-bold), single font, no gradients, no drop shadows beyond shadow-sm on active segment thumbs.

CONTEXT-AWARE CONTENTS: the FRAME is constant (left identity cluster, right cluster) so it never feels like a different page. Only the contextual middle/right swap by mode — Run shows role segment + live actions; Setup hides the role segment (shows "Setup mode" label) and the right cluster shows Save/Preview/identity-edit. Implement as a controlled component: RunMode and SetupMode each pass their own props object to ONE bar wrapper — no `if mode===` branching inside the bar.
synthesis.bodySpec:
TWO-COLUMN BROADCAST DESK (desktop md+) | SINGLE FULL-BLEED DECK (mobile, md:hidden).

DESKTOP (md+): CSS grid, two columns under the unified bar. LEFT = GAME CONTROL (flex-grow, ~60%), RIGHT = PRESENTATION (fixed ~300–340px, collapses to a drawer below 1024px if tight).

LEFT COLUMN — GAME CONTROL (logic 100% untouched)
- Scoreboard hero: RunInteractiveScoreboard exactly as-is (Home / Clock / Away tiles, 24–32px hero score).
- Clock control + segment/period control — as-is.
- Per-side stat steppers (Shots / Exclusions / Timeouts etc.) — per-team + game-scope steppers, the existing useConsoleFit density-downshift behavior preserved.
- (Roster + Celebrate/Cue clusters MAY stay left under the scoreboard OR move right with Presentation — see control map; default: cues stay near game state on the left, roster moves to a right-column accordion. Either is acceptable; the mock shows roster right.)

RIGHT COLUMN — PRESENTATION (the home Level C folds into; vMix Program-bus treatment)
Rendered top-to-bottom:
1. PROGRAM BUS header strip: "Show on board" label (Tv icon) + Back-to-Live button. Back-to-Live is the broadcast "Take" equivalent — ALWAYS present: green/emerald "Live" (board already live, disabled) → loud red "Back to live" when a scene is on-air. (Existing ShowControlPanel logic.)
2. Scene tiles — VERTICAL stack (not a horizontal strip): Halftime / Lineup / Sponsors / This Week / Countdown, one full-width tile each. The on-air scene wears the TALLY treatment: indigo bg + an "ON AIR" tally ring/outline + label (the vMix Program highlight). Tap = take(templateId). When a scene is on-air: countdown chip ("Back to live in 0:18") + Hold + Extend(+20s) buttons appear inline beneath it.
3. Ribbon live preview — small iframe/preview of what's currently on the LED ribbon, co-located with scene control.
4. Celebrate cues — inline cue tiles (Goal / Save / Exclusion / Power Play / Horn, per-sport) — the CueLaunchpad, reused.
5. Ribbon control — collapsible accordion (Presets / Messages / Images).
6. Roster — collapsible accordion (Home lineup / Away lineup).

BOTTOM (full-width, both columns): Recent events / Undo trail — pinned scrollable event list with per-row Undo. Spans the desk width.

MOBILE (md:hidden) — SINGLE FULL-BLEED SCROLLING DECK via the existing md:contents linearization pattern, runs at 320px:
- The unified bar becomes a sticky compact header (identity + LIVE chip + Open ▾ + screens nub + Send). Role segments scroll INTO the top of the deck (horizontal-scroll segmented control), not a second bar.
- Score + clock = sticky/pinned at top of the deck (operator must never scroll past a live event).
- Below, in scroll order: scene tiles (Program bus) → ribbon preview → celebrate cues → roster → ribbon control. One unit, one scroll.
- Pinned bottom status bar: recent-events / undo strip + screens nub mirror.
- NO second or third bar EVER appears on mobile. Deck target: ≤2 screen-heights of primary content; verified on iPhone 12 (390px) and iPad Air landscape (820px, where the two-column desk engages).

synthesis.mockSpec:
BUILD A HIGH-FIDELITY STATIC HTML APPROVAL MOCK (single self-contained file, real Google Font, Tailwind-equivalent inline styles or CDN Tailwind). Render BOTH a desktop view (1440×900) and a stacked mobile view (390×844) on the same page so Greg signs off on one artifact. Use a concrete LIVE-GAME EXAMPLE throughout (see below). NOT a wireframe — real shadows, real type, real colors, real spacing.

EXACT EXAMPLE TO RENDER (water polo, mid-game, one screen down — exercises every state):
- Game: "Lincoln vs Roosevelt" · status = LIVE (red pulsing chip).
- Mode = Run. Role = Show Caller selected (indigo thumb on 3rd segment).
- Score hero: HOME Lincoln 8 — Q3 4:12 (clock running) — AWAY Roosevelt 6.
- Stat steppers below: Shots 14/11, Exclusions 2/3, Timeouts 1/2.
- Penalty pill ACTIVE: ⏱ with amber fill + count badge "1".
- Screens nub ESCALATED: red dot + "3/4" (one screen frozen) — shows the severity roll-up in its alarm state.
- Right column Program bus: "Sponsors" scene ON AIR (indigo tile + ON-AIR tally ring), countdown "Back to live in 0:14", Hold + +20s buttons showing; Back-to-Live button in loud RED. Other tiles (Halftime / Lineup / This Week / Countdown) quiet white.
- Ribbon preview: a thin LED-ribbon strip showing a sponsor message.
- Celebrate cues row: Goal · Save · Exclusion · Power Play · Horn.
- Bottom undo trail: "8–6 Lincoln goal (#7) · 12s ago [Undo]", "Exclusion Roosevelt #4 · 0:48 ago [Undo]".

LAYOUT ZONES (desktop):
- TOP: the unified 48px bar, full width. LEFT cluster: ArrowLeft chip · [Run|Set up] segmented (Run active, green pulse) · "Lincoln vs Roosevelt" bold · LIVE chip (red, pulsing dot, ⌄). CENTER: [Full|Scorekeeper|Show Caller|PA] segmented, Show Caller = indigo. RIGHT: Star · ⏱1 (amber) · ●3/4 (red nub) · ExternalLink · [Open ▾]. One row, no wrap. Border-bottom only; NO inter-zone borders.
- BODY grid: LEFT ~840px Game Control (scoreboard hero + steppers + undo trail can sit bottom-left or full-width bottom), RIGHT ~340px Presentation (Program bus header w/ red Back-to-Live, vertical scene tiles w/ Sponsors ON AIR tally, countdown+Hold+20s, ribbon preview, celebrate cues, Ribbon + Roster accordions collapsed).

MOBILE view (390px): sticky compact header (identity + LIVE + ●3/4 + ExternalLink + Open ▾) → horizontal-scroll role segment → pinned score/clock → scene tiles (Sponsors ON AIR) → ribbon preview → celebrate cues → accordions → pinned bottom undo strip. ONE column, ONE scroll, NO second bar.

TOKENS: font Inter (or system Anthropic Sans stand-in), weights 400/700. Colors: slate-100 #f1f5f9 / slate-200 #e2e8f0 / slate-500 #64748b / slate-600 #475569 / slate-900 #0f172a; indigo-600 #4f46e5 (active role + send hover ONLY); red-600 #dc2626 (LIVE + Back-to-live + frozen nub); amber-500 #f59e0b (penalty + showing-other); green-500 #22c55e (healthy); emerald-100 bg for the disabled 'Live' state. Radii: rounded-xl on segmented containers, rounded-lg on buttons, rounded-full on chips/pills. Active segment thumb: white bg + shadow-sm. Scene ON-AIR tally: 2px indigo ring + indigo bg. NO backdrop-blur anywhere. NO gradients. NO drop shadows except shadow-sm on thumbs and the right-column elevation. Type scale: 13px control labels, 11px chip caps (uppercase tracking-widest), 9px sublabels, 24–32px hero score, line-height 1.2. Icons 18px in the bar, 16px in body chips. Annotate the mock with small callout pins: "1 — context/nav", "2 — role (rationed indigo)", "3 — live+ambient", "4 — Program bus / on-air tally", "5 — Back-to-Live = Take" so Greg can map zones at a glance.
sliceOrder: SLICE 1 — Unified bar adoption (reuse, no logic change): RunCommandBar already IS the three-zone bar. Pull Back-to-GameDay + Run/Setup segmented + the four surface popouts down out of the page header (page.tsx ~529-614) INTO the bar's left zone (back+mode) and right-zone Open ▾ menu. Wire the status chip's tap to open the RunStatusControl transition menu (chip = indicator + trigger). Hide the role segment when mode=Setup. Net: page header (Level A) is deleted; one bar remains.
